extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media professionals, researchers, and readers interested in scientific publishing and research integrity
extracted.subtask_description: A journal press release announcing the retraction of a published clinical trial, explaining the reasons for retraction, the investigative process, and guidance to the media and readers about use of the study findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to statistical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns about the approach to statistical analysis of the data were raised as a substantive problem with the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical issues (including analytical errors) undermine the validity of results; journals should refer analyses to statistical experts, attempt replication, and consider corrective action when serious problems are found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implausible statistical values
rubrics_metrics.description: The study contained implausible statistical values that called its findings into question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of implausible or internally inconsistent statistical values warrants expert review and can form part of the justification for retraction if they cannot be reconciled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability and authenticity of raw data
rubrics_metrics.description: Irregularities in the raw dataset and questions about the authenticity/reliability of underlying data were identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When raw data show irregularities or cannot be authenticated, independent scrutiny is required; unresolved data integrity problems can lead to retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate reporting of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The methods were inadequately reported, limiting the ability to assess or replicate the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insufficient methodological reporting impedes verification and may justify correction or retraction, since transparent methods are necessary for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of prospective trial registration (editorial policy breach)
rubrics_metrics.description: The study lacked prospective trial registration, which breaches BMJ Group’s editorial policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective registration of clinical trials is an editorial requirement; failure to register prospectively is a serious policy breach and can be grounds for rejecting publication or for reassessing published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial concerns raised via critiques and letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns were first raised in critiques of the study, some published as letters in the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-publication critiques and letters can trigger formal investigation; journals should pay attention to substantive community-voiced concerns as part of content integrity procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content integrity investigation process
rubrics_metrics.description: BMJ Group’s content integrity team reviews concerns, refers to statistical experts, attempts to replicate results, examines data authenticity, and corresponds with researchers and institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should follow due process, include independent expert assessment and replication attempts where appropriate, and may require detailed data and correspondence review; such investigations can take several months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency via appended expert reports
rubrics_metrics.description: An expert/statistical report was appended to the retraction notice describing the findings of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing independent expert reports alongside retraction notices promotes transparency and informs readers about the basis for the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' response and agreement to retract
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors stated the identified errors were honest mistakes and agreed with the decision to retract the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors' acknowledgement or agreement can be noted in retraction communications, but the decision to retract is based on the integrity and reliability of the work rather than solely on authors' statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance to media on citing retracted research
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists and others should no longer reference or use the study findings in future reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When research is retracted, media and communicators should cease citing or relying on the findings and should correct prior coverage where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility to correct the scientific record
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal emphasises acting in the interests of openness and the importance of correcting the scientific record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should proactively investigate credible concerns and act to correct or retract work when evidence shows results are unreliable, balancing speed with thorough, fair process.
